title: ABS: safety and agility in one plane
lesson_en: Compare two competing objectives directly. These error bars show standard deviations, not confidence intervals.

title: RC-PPO: aligned horizontal method comparisons
lesson_en: Horizontal method labels and repeated panels make comparisons easier. The caption defines the error bars as standard errors.

title: RC-PPO: cost and reachability viewed together
lesson_en: Place task completion and cumulative cost next to one another. The cost statistic here is IQM, not a simple mean.

title: RC-PPO: tested settings in a trade-off plot
lesson_en: A trade-off view examines whether a result is explained by baseline tuning. A few points alone cannot establish a theoretical Pareto frontier.

title: rliable: horizontal interval estimates across metrics
lesson_en: Use aligned rows to compare multiple metrics with less visual ink. Intervals are stratified-bootstrap 95% confidence intervals from original runs.

title: Safety-Gymnasium: performance and constraint compliance
lesson_en: Give performance and safety separate roles. Its cost-category stacks are disjoint; collision and budget violations in our task may overlap.

title: Resilient: a compact ablation comparison
lesson_en: A small set of variants can work well in grouped bars. Its collision-recovery task and standard-deviation bars have different meanings from our task.

title: Risk-aware locomotion: three metrics over one parameter
lesson_en: Parameter curves expose performance, termination, and tracking trade-offs. These 95% intervals cover evaluation spawns for a single trained seed.

title: Risk-aware locomotion: mean and tail under perturbations
lesson_en: Repeated panels separate physical perturbations and compare mean and tail performance. Do not import its CVaR parameter as our cost margin alpha.

title: AutoRL: fewer methods in scenario comparisons
lesson_en: Grouped bars remain readable when each panel has a clear question and a limited method set.

title: AutoRL: explicit noise-response curves
lesson_en: Use curves when the horizontal axis is a meaningful ordered physical variable. Unordered scene names should not imply an interpolated trend.

title: Confined spaces: operating boundaries as heatmaps
lesson_en: A method-by-difficulty heatmap reveals the operating boundary. Different metric units need separate panels and color scales.

title: NoMaD: a compact multi-metric result table
lesson_en: A table can communicate all baseline values directly, leaving figures to explain behavior. Collisions here are mean counts, not collision rates.

title: SEA-Nav: metrics grouped by environment difficulty
lesson_en: Scene groups make a dense comparison structured. This excerpt is the archived v1; an online v2 exists and is recorded separately in the manifest.

title: iPlanner: scene comparisons in a small table
lesson_en: A small table is often sufficient for complete scene-by-method comparisons; do not repeat every cell as a bar.

title: ViPlanner: scene blocks with different metrics
lesson_en: Keep scene groups and metric units explicit. This is a layout reference, not evidence that its loss metrics equal our execution cost.

title: VAPOR: navigation performance across four scenarios
lesson_en: A full metric table complements qualitative routes. Current consumption, normalized trajectory length, and success have distinct meanings.

title: ViNT: a quantitative table paired with trajectories
lesson_en: Let a compact comparison table report numbers while a trajectory view explains the observed navigation behavior.

title: ActSafe: reward, cost, and an explicit safety limit
lesson_en: Align performance and constraint curves and draw the limit explicitly. These learning curves and standard errors require training histories.
